title: Squintum Dramatic Club
text:
SQUINTUM DRAMATIC CLUB

Following the destruction of the buildings in 1890, funds were raised and new buildings were erected in 1891, at which time the school changed from a privately owned to an Independent School, Professor Halsell and some of his former teachers continuing with the new school for a brief period.

In 1891 a group of students and public spirited citizens formed an amateur organization, named themselves the "Squintum Dramatic Club," and gave a number of plays for the purpose of raising funds for the purchase of a new bell for the school. Harry Naylor (now deceased) and Robert Naylor, brothers, residing at Collinsville, were prime movers in the organization of this club. The bell was purchased and presented to the school that year, and is now given an honored place in the present building, which is a successor to the one built in 1891.

The club was organized at the home of Mr. and Mrs. J. E. Squires on November 13, 1890, with thirteen members. Officers then elected were Eldridge K. Norsworthy, chairman; Pinkney E. Durrett, treasurer; Gus W. Thomasson, secretary. A committee on plays and parts was appointed, consisting of Robert F. Naylor, Claude C. Hodge, Miss Jennie Lacy and Miss Stella Anderson. The object of the club was stated as being "to organize for the purpose of giving an entertainment in the interest of raising funds to purchase a bell for the new college, now in course of construction." The old Savoy Hotel was selected as headquarters of the club. Later, the meeting place was changed to the "new school house." Allie G. Hughes and Gus W. Thomasson were appointed chief janitors.

At a meeting held on November 20 a play was selected titled, "Out in the Streets," and another titled "Joke on Squintum," with a tableau, "Woman's Rights." Thus, began the activities of the club. Early in the program, Mrs. J. E. Squires was delegated the authority to assign play parts. Will H. Davis was selected as curtain manager with Ed A. McMahon as his assistant.
notes: After the 1890 fire, the school rebuilt in 1891 and became an independent (public) school. The Squintum Dramatic Club raised funds for a new college bell.
